libs/kotaemon/kotaemon/llms/chats/langch.loses: Only the OpenAI and Anthropic SDK clients that a LangChain object holds actually route -- wrap_langchain finds and wraps those specifically, and no-ops for the Azure/Gemini/Cohere/Ollama clients also reachable through this same line, so those keep today's direct-provider behavior unchanged. For the OpenAI/Anthropic calls that do route, the same per-call fallback and Router-default-service-tier trade-offs described at openai.py:308 apply, since wrap_langchain installs the identical transport under the hood.
libs/kotaemon/kotaemon/llms/chats/langch.why: LCChatMixin.__init__ builds self._obj = self._lc_class(**params) dynamically (the actual class -- langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI, ChatAnthropic, AzureChatOpenAI, ChatGoogleGenerativeAI, ChatCohere, or ChatOllama -- is only known at runtime via _get_lc_class(), so the scanner can't see this site). Passed the built object through router_runtime.wrap_langchain(), which finds and wraps whichever real OpenAI/Anthropic SDK client the LangChain object holds (root_client/_client/etc) and no-ops for everything else. Verified with `check --run`: both LCChatOpenAI and LCAnthropicChat sent valid /v1/responses and /v1/messages requests to the Router simulator respectively (2 valid, 0 invalid). LCAzureChatOpenAI, LCGeminiChat, LCCohereChat and LCOllamaChat pass through this same line unaffected, since wrap_langchain only acts on openai/anthropic client instances -- Gemini/Cohere/Ollama have no Router endpoint, and Azure keeps the same hard limit as above.

libs/kotaemon/kotaemon/llms/chats/openai.loses: Calls using a param Router can't translate for Chat Completions (seed, n>1, logprobs/top_logprobs, a tool_choice of a non-function type, a message with a 'name' field, max_tokens<16, audio/modalities/prediction/web_search_options/logit_bias, or a dated/retired model id not in Router's catalog) fall back to OpenAI unchanged, so this wrap only changes behavior for calls Router can actually serve. Those calls get Router's account-default service tier (Flex pricing/latency where the model offers it, unless ROUTER_MIGRATE_SERVICE_TIER pins a tier) instead of OpenAI's own default tier, and any `stop` sequence is now cut out of the text client-side by the runtime instead of being truncated server-side by OpenAI.
libs/kotaemon/kotaemon/llms/chats/openai.why: ChatOpenAI.prepare_client (async): wrapped the AsyncOpenAI client with router_runtime.wrap_openai() so its chat.completions.create traffic routes through Router when RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY is set. wrap_openai falls back to OpenAI untouched for anything Router can't serve (dated models, seed, n>1, etc).

libs/kotaemon/kotaemon/llms/chats/openai.why: StructuredOutputChatOpenAI.aopenai_response: inherits the async wrap from openai.py:308 the same way.

AzureChatOpenAI.openai_response calls client.chat.completions.create, but the client is built by AzureChatOpenAI.prepare_client (openai.py:467-473) as openai.AzureOpenAI/AsyncAzureOpenAI, keyed by azure_endpoint + azure_deployment + api_version rather than a model id. router_runtime.wrap_openai() explicitly refuses to wrap AzureOpenAI/AsyncAzureOpenAI clients ('Azure deployments and test doubles stay on their configured endpoint') and `router-migrate wrap` itself reports 'AsyncAzureOpenAI (azure-openai) has no deterministic wrap'. Router has no Azure-shaped endpoint (no azure_endpoint/deployment/api_version concept), so this call physically can't be routed without the operator reconfiguring deployments to point at Router, which is a deployment/infra decision, not a code change. A human would need to decide whether to stop using the Azure-specific client (switching the azure_deployment to a Router catalog model id via the plain ChatOpenAI/base_url path instead) if they want this traffic on Router.
AzureChatOpenAI.aopenai_response: same Azure client as openai.py:502 above; same hard limit.
